title_text: What is oxytocin and why is it important?
content_text: Let’s talk about oxytocin: the hormone of love. This little marvel is linked to attachment, happiness, love, and even orgasms. When the end of pregnancy approaches and your baby is about to make an appearance, oxytocin levels skyrocket. Oxytocin is like the conductor that prepares your body for childbirth, leading the way for those powerful uterine contractions. Once the baby says hello to the world, oxytocin rises even more to help expel the placenta. But there are certain factors that can play tricks on oxytocin production during childbirth. Fear, anxiety, anesthesia, or even anger can reduce oxytocin levels, and that’s when the doctor steps in with synthetic oxytocin, also known as Pitocin. But wait, there’s more! Oxytocin doesn’t just stop at welcoming the baby. Have you ever wondered why you feel that instant love and deep connection with your little one? It’s thanks to oxytocin! Furthermore, this hormone is also behind the magic of breastfeeding, making the milk flow so your baby can enjoy their feast. The production of the “hormone of love” plays a starring role in our physical and psychological life. It doesn’t only allow babies to come into the world, but also promotes that special care and attachment with their mother, increasing the chances of survival. Oxytocin, always giving us good vibes and making us feel on cloud nine!
